newsitem.title: SPAIN: Two bombs explode on beaches in western Spain.
newsitem.headline: Two bombs explode on beaches in western Spain.

text.p: Two bombs exploded on Wednesday on beaches along Spain's eastern coast, causing no damage or injury, Catalonia region officials said.
The bombs went off at 8.00 a.m. and 8.30 a.m. while leaders of the NATO military alliance were meeting in Madrid more than 600 km (375 miles) away.
Officials did not say whether Basque separatist rebels ETA were responsible, but the group often sets off small bombs at tourist sites during the summer season.

On Tuesday, police evacuated 15,000 sunbathers from Lloret de Mar beaches in the same area north of Barcelona after a caller in the name of ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) warned that the group had planted a bomb.
Security in Madrid was at a maximum because of fears of an attack by the separatist group during the two-day NATO summit.
ETA has killed some 800 people during its nearly 30-year campaign for an independent Basque state.
